clue.text: It will cause distress to criticise severely

definitions.meaning: to upset someone badly is to leave them hurt and wounded in spirit
to savage a book or play in a review, slashing it to pieces

explanation.surface: Harsh criticism is said to be upsetting.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to wound someone emotionally and to slate them in a review.

clue.text: Dawn has two birds

parts.note: a cock is a male fowl
a crow is a black corvid

explanation.surface: Daybreak brings a pair of birds.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase supplies both pieces: two bird names side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The rooster's call marks first light, so the phrase is a poetic word for daybreak.

clue.text: Blamed ironically despite having expressed gratitude

definitions.meaning: saying 'thanks a lot' sarcastically lays blame on someone

explanation.surface: Someone was criticised even though they had said thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratitude spoken sarcastically ('thanks for nothing') amounts to a reproach, giving both senses.

clue.text: With which to spear a fish

definitions.meaning: a long-shafted infantry weapon with a pointed head

explanation.surface: Asking what tool one uses to spear a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the old foot-soldier's spear and a toothy freshwater predator.

clue.text: Mysterious, strange coteries

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters of the next word are oddly reordered

explanation.surface: Exclusive little social circles are odd and secretive.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is understood only by a small initiated circle, hence obscure or arcane.

clue.text: Used transport

parts.note: vehicles that have had a previous owner, sold on a forecourt

explanation.definitionFit: Pre-owned motor vehicles are means of getting about that have already been driven by someone else.

clue.text: Short story about powder found in the bathroom

indicators.note: short means the word for story loses its final letter

parts.note: a tale is a story
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A brief anecdote concerning toiletries kept by the bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' docks the last letter of TALE, giving TAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Talcum powder is a soft mineral dusting powder kept for use after bathing.

clue.text: Diana performing in extremes of restraint is shining brightly

indicators.note: in places the rearranged name within the outer letters
extremes of picks out the first and last letters of the following word
performing suggests the name is active and moved about, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A performer named Diana, though restrained, is glowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performing' rearranges DIANA to ADIAN, which goes 'in' R and T, the first and last letters of 'restraint' picked out by 'extremes of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiant describes something emitting light or glowing with brightness.

clue.text: Caught girl on Scottish island

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Anna is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is caught out on a Hebridean island.
explanation.walkthrough: Canna is one of the Small Isles of the Inner Hebrides, off Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small Hebridean isle near Rum and Skye, west of mainland Scotland.

clue.text: Sailor in a precious suit?

parts.note: a sailor is a jack tar, and the suit of playing cards named after gemstones is precious

explanation.definitionFit: The court card is the knave belonging to the suit marked with red gemstone shapes.

clue.text: Plant bird in American intelligence unit

indicators.note: in places the bird inside the agency's initials

parts.note: the CIA is the Central Intelligence Agency
a lark is a songbird

explanation.surface: Spies in Washington plant a bird in their agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarkia is a genus of annual flowering garden plants from western North America.

clue.text: Young boy once going round broke the pottery

indicators.note: going round means the rearranged letters surround the youngster
broke suggests the word once is smashed and its letters scattered

parts.note: a lad is a young boy

explanation.surface: A child long ago broke the crockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' looks like 'formerly' but is anagram fodder for 'broke', making CEON; 'going round' wraps that around the youngster. 'Celadon' names the grey-green glazed ware.
explanation.definitionFit: Celadon is a pale grey-green glazed ceramic ware, originally from China.

clue.text: Food for a ruler in the establishment

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the abbreviation

parts.note: the Church of England, CE, is the established church
K is short for king

explanation.surface: Provisions for a monarch within an institution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the establishment' is the Church of England, the state church; A and K go 'in' CE.
explanation.definitionFit: A baked sweet confection is something to eat.

clue.text: But you will not have to sniff out this animal

definitions.text: But you will not have to sniff out this animal

parts.words: But you will not have to sniff out this animal
parts.note: a creature whose powerful smell announces itself, so no hunting by nose is needed

explanation.definitionFit: This black-and-white mammal sprays a pungent stinking fluid, so its presence is obvious to the nose.

clue.text: Animal heard by priest in Tibet

indicators.note: heard means the word for the animal is said out loud

parts.note: a llama is a woolly South American animal

explanation.surface: A creature is listened to by a Tibetan cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: A lama is a Buddhist spiritual teacher or monk in Tibetan Buddhism.

clue.text: Try to get in touch

parts.note: reads like making contact, but means feeling about blindly with the hands

explanation.definitionFit: To feel one's way searchingly with the hands is to attempt to find something by contact.

clue.text: Black magic?

parts.note: sorcery practised in the Caribbean, with a hint that the word looks like a magic word

explanation.definitionFit: Obeah is a form of sorcery or witchcraft practised in parts of the West Indies.

clue.text: Form of ceremony dirty boys often do not like

definitions.text: Form of ceremony dirty boys often do not like

parts.words: Form of ceremony dirty boys often do not like
parts.note: an order of knighthood read as an instruction to go and wash

explanation.walkthrough: The British honour is an order of chivalry; read literally, it is an order to wash.
explanation.definitionFit: The honour is a British order of chivalry conferred at a formal investiture, punning on a command to bathe.

clue.text: Rose as many reached a conclusion

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword convention for many
ended means finished or reached a conclusion

explanation.surface: A rose grew while many came to a decision.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose here is the past tense of rise, meaning went upwards.

clue.text: Forms of take-over?

parts.note: documents completed when a family takes over a child, not a company

explanation.definitionFit: The legal documents for taking a child into one's family as one's own are official paperwork.

clue.text: Pertaining to the lower parts in the main

definitions.text: Pertaining to the lower parts in the main

parts.words: Pertaining to the lower parts in the main
parts.note: the main is an old poetic word for the ocean, so this is about its depths

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the deepest reaches of the ocean far below the surface.

clue.text: Burning sensation felt in range in one sense

parts.note: a feeling felt in the ears, the organs of hearing
hot describes a burning sensation

explanation.surface: Somebody feels a burning sensation.
explanation.walkthrough: Ears burning is said of someone being talked about; here the hot sensation is felt in the ears.
explanation.definitionFit: Earshot is the distance within which sounds can be heard, a range for hearing.

clue.text: Better abstainer leaves this

indicators.note: leaves means the abstainer departs from the word better

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means an abstainer from alcohol

explanation.surface: A non-drinker is wise to leave alcohol alone.
explanation.walkthrough: With TT gone from BETTER, what is left is what a teetotaller leaves alone: the whole clue defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: A teetotaller shuns alcoholic drink such as ale and lager.

clue.text: Singer included one principal ingredient

indicators.note: included means the singer's voice holds the numeral within it

parts.note: a bass is a low-voiced male singer
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A vocalist was part of the main mixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A basis is the chief component or foundation of something.

clue.text: Taste a kiss

definitions.meaning: a loud kiss on the lips

explanation.surface: Sampling a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a distinctive flavour and a noisy smacker of a kiss.

clue.text: Deliver without charge

explanation.surface: Delivery at no cost.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to liberate someone and gratis, at no cost.

clue.text: Beat worker first with restraint

indicators.note: first means the worker comes before the beat in the answer

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
to cuff is to strike with an open hand

explanation.surface: A worker is struck before being restrained.
explanation.definitionFit: Handcuffs are a lockable restraint fastened round a prisoner's wrists.

clue.text: See 25
Hold up involving you and me in a spot

indicators.note: involving means the stain wraps round the pronoun

parts.note: a stain is a spot or mark
us means you and me

explanation.surface: A robbery that gets the two of us into trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain is to support or bear the weight of something.

clue.text: Without it, lived without even the ordinary comforts when ruffled

indicators.note: without means the little word is removed from the phrase

parts.words: lived without even the ordinary comforts
parts.note: to rough it is to live without basic comforts

explanation.surface: Someone who lived spartanly was put out by it.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'roughed it' means lived without comforts; drop IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Roughed means ruffled up, as hair or feathers made untidy.

clue.text: Careless friends returning have to hurry

indicators.note: returning means the word for friends is read backwards

parts.note: pals are friends
to dash is to hurry

explanation.surface: Thoughtless mates who come back must rush off.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash work is done hastily and carelessly, without attention to detail.

clue.text: Overweight boy was doomed

parts.note: fat means overweight
Ed is a boy's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: A heavy lad had no hope.
explanation.definitionFit: If something was fated, destiny had sealed it, so it was doomed.
